report.headline: Sword Knight's installs collapsed after Nov 1 (419 → 60 a day) and day-1 retention of 19% can't hold the player base without them.
report.overview: Both games are new and small. Sword Knight averaged 453 daily users this week (double the week before), but its new installs fell sharply from Nov 2 and daily users dropped to 220 by Nov 4. Jelly Kitchen is climbing from launch (218 daily users on Nov 4) but keeps only 14% of players to day 1 and sends none of its own game events to Firebase, so its levels are invisible. Ad revenue is $15.40 for Sword Knight and $0.03 for Jelly Kitchen this week.

games.summary: Installs peaked at 419 on Nov 1 and fell to 60 on Nov 4, taking daily users from 631 to 220. Retention is weak (D1 19%, D7 3.4%), so the game shrinks as soon as installs slow. Ad revenue rose 10× from Oct 31 but is still about $0.01 per daily user.
highlights: Avg daily users 453 vs 221 the week before (+105%).
Ad revenue $15.40 vs $1.34; daily revenue jumped from about $0.30 to about $3 on Oct 31.
Minutes per daily user up from 5.5 to 7.8.
Unfinished levels down: level_end / level_start is 71% vs 62% the week before.
concerns: New installs: 419 (Nov 1) → 254 → 106 → 60 (Nov 4). Check whether a campaign stopped or ran out of budget.
Day-1 retention 19% and day-7 3.4%, far below the 30%+ day-1 casual games need.
Rewarded ads: 8,564 adoffer events but only 145 ad_reward (about 2%).
Top countries are low-value for ads (India, Iran, Myanmar, Iraq, Pakistan); 196 players are in Iran, where AdMob doesn't serve ads.
Duplicate events (ad_reward / ad_rewardreceived, ad_click / ad_clicked), and tutorial fired only 5 times while ftue fired 8,203.
actions: Find out why installs dropped on Nov 2 (campaign paused, budget, or store listing change).
Look at the first session: where do the 81% who don't return on day 1 stop? Add an ftue step parameter if it's missing.
Check what changed in ads on Oct 31 and whether interstitial frequency is now hurting retention.
Make rewarded offers more valuable or show them at better moments; confirm adoffer fires only when the player actually sees the offer.
Remove the duplicate ad events, and roll 1.3.x out to more players (2,080 are still on 1.1.0).

games.summary: Live since Oct 28 and growing: 656 installs this week and 218 daily users on Nov 4. Day-1 retention is 13.7% and players spend only 2.5 minutes a day. Firebase receives no level or booster events, so difficulty problems can't be seen yet.
highlights: 187 installs on Nov 4, the best day so far.
concerns: 2.5 minutes per daily user and 1.34 sessions per daily user: most players leave quickly.
Only 14 of 654 players saw an ad (63 impressions, $0.03).
No custom events at all: no level_start, level_complete, level_fail or booster_use.
actions: Connect the game's analytics events (Analytics.Sink) to Firebase so level starts, wins and fails are tracked; rename session_start, which Firebase reserves.
Check why ads reach so few players (ads not loading, or shown too late in the level order).
Review the first 2-3 minutes of play; most players leave before then.
